title: ASX Group Dealing Rules Policy (Version 8.0)

tiers.name: ASX People
tiers.description: All ASX people including fixed-term staff, direct contractors, casuals, secondees, consultants deemed subject to the Policy by People and Culture, and ASX Group directors. Must pre-clear all dealing in Covered Securities, may deal in ASX Group Securities only in a designated ASX Trading Window, must deal within five business days of clearance, and are subject to the three-month short-term dealing ban, the hedging ban over unvested and holding-locked securities and the collateral ban.

tiers.name: ASX Group Executives
tiers.description: ASX Group Executives. Distinguished only by the obligation to notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities, which may be publicly disclosed.

tiers.name: ASX Group Directors
tiers.description: ASX Group directors. Subject to the whole Policy as ASX People, plus the notification to the Company Secretary of any derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. Pre-clearance for ASX Limited NEDs comes from the Chair of ASX Limited (alternate: Group General Counsel or Chief Risk Officer); the Chair of ASX Limited is cleared by the Chair of the Board Risk Committee.

tiers.name: ASX Limited and CS facility licensee Non-Executive Directors
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors of ASX Limited and of the CS facility licensees. The Policy's restrictions apply to them only in relation to ASX Group Securities and no pre-clearance is needed for non-ASX Group Securities. All their dealings in ASX Group Securities must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days whether or not the beneficial holding changes, and short-term dealing within three months is prohibited.

tiers.name: NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors on the boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees. Prohibited from holding ASX Group securities at all; those holding on appointment must divest promptly and in compliance with the Policy.

tiers.name: Chief Compliance Officer and people in Listings Compliance, the Market Announcements Office and Surveillance
tiers.description: Must not hold, deal in or have an interest in Covered Securities, except securities held before appointment (which may be held but not dealt), corporate actions on pre-held securities, acceptance of a takeover or scheme, participation in ASX Employee Share Plans, and dealing in ASX Group securities in a designated Trading Window with pre-clearance.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: An ASX person's spouse, de facto partner, children residing with them, and companies, trusts, Self-Managed Super Funds or other entities controlled by the ASX person and/or their Connected Persons. ASX People must take reasonable steps to inform them of the Policy and ensure they comply with it as if they were the ASX person.

definitions.hedging_definition: a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock

windows.start_anchor: the day after release of ASX's half-year results
the day after release of ASX's full-year results
the day after ASX's Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The ASX Board determines ASX Trading Windows from time to time, may decline to open a Trading Window at any of the three ordinary times, and may elect to shorten, change or close a Trading Window at any time. In addition, pre-clearance to deal may be denied for any reason, expressly including 'matters known to ASX, but not to you', so a confidential prohibition can be applied at the individual level.

rules.section: 2.5 (Derivatives and hedging arrangements over ASX Group Securities)
rules.detail: Absolute ban on any transaction limiting the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities, with no venue limit and no approval route. A collar is squarely a transaction that limits economic risk.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The ban expressly extends to vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock, so the collar pool must be limited to vested shares free of any holding lock.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked ASX Group Securities is expressly contemplated rather than prohibited. The only stated requirement for directors is notification to the Company Secretary, and the position may be publicly disclosed. Pre-clearance under section 2.2 is expressed to apply to dealing in Covered Securities, which are financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, so an over-the-counter hedge is not itself a Covered Security, but the Policy requires compliance with its spirit as well as its letter.
rules.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.

rules.detail: Same position as directors: permitted over vested unlocked securities, subject to notifying the Company Secretary and possible public disclosure. No deadline or form is specified for the notification.
rules.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities.

rules.detail: A put, call or collar over unvested or holding-locked ASX Group Securities limits economic risk and is caught by the express prohibition, whatever the venue.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options, warrants, futures and derivatives quoted on an Australian financial market are Covered Securities, so dealing in them requires pre-clearance through the online form, must be executed within five business days, and, where they are over ASX Group Securities, only in a designated ASX Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, including shares, debentures and hybrids, warrants, futures, options, derivatives and single-entity Exchange Traded Products (ETPs) ... You must not deal in Covered Securities without ASX pre-clearance approval.

rules.detail: An over-the-counter put or call is not quoted on an Australian financial market and so is not a Covered Security or a Security as defined, meaning the pre-clearance machinery does not by its terms bite on the derivative itself. What the Policy does require is notification to the Company Secretary of a derivative position over vested ASX Group Securities.
rules.evidence: Securities: Any financial product quoted on a financial market.

rules.tier: NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees
rules.detail: These directors may not hold ASX Group securities at all and must divest any held on appointment, so there is no shareholding over which a collar could be written.
rules.evidence: For NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees, the holding of ASX Group securities is prohibited (with any directors who hold ASX Group Securities prior to their appointment being required to divest those shares promptly and compliantly with this Policy).

rules.section: 2.5 (ASX Group Securities margin loans and other financing arrangements)
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. Any monetisation that advances cash against the shares is a financing arrangement, and using ASX Group Securities as collateral for it is prohibited outright. An unsecured cash-settled monetisation would instead be treated as a hedging or derivative position requiring notification by executives and directors.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy. A short position would in practice be caught by the three-month purchase-then-sale prohibition and by the requirement to pre-clear dealing in Covered Securities.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of Deal, which is confined to buying, acquiring, selling, transferring, disposing or converting Covered Securities or agreeing to do so.

Contracts for difference are not named. They are not quoted on an Australian financial market and so are not Covered Securities, but a CFD over unvested or holding-locked ASX Group Securities would be caught by the ban on transactions limiting economic risk.

Flat ban on using ASX Group Securities as collateral for a new margin loan, with an added obligation to ensure that any portfolio of Covered Securities given as collateral contains no ASX Group Securities. Margin loans and financing over non-ASX Group Securities do not even require pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement. You must ensure any portfolio of Covered Securities provided as collateral does not comprise ASX Group Securities.

rules.detail: Pledging or charging ASX Group Securities to any financier is prohibited because it is the use of those securities as collateral. The prohibition is framed by reference to entering a new margin loan or financing arrangement, so an encumbrance unconnected with financing is not expressly addressed, and creating a security interest is not itself within the definition of Deal.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin loans; it reaches any 'other financing arrangement' collateralised by ASX Group Securities, applies to all ASX people and their Connected Persons and to all vesting states, and applies to new arrangements. There is no approval route, although the section 2.8 waiver power is expressed to cover the Policy's dealing prohibitions generally.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement.

rules.detail: No purchase then sale, or sale then purchase, of Covered Securities of the same entity within three months. Market volatility is expressly rejected as a ground for exemption, and dealing that ASX considers frequent may also be denied clearance.
rules.evidence: You must not purchase then sell (and inversely sell and then purchase) any Covered Securities of the same entity within a three-month period. Market volatility will not be considered as a reason for exemption from this prohibition

rules.tier: ASX Limited and CS facility licensee Non-Executive Directors
rules.detail: Restated for NEDs in relation to ASX Group Securities specifically.
rules.evidence: Short-term dealing (that is, within a three-month period) in ASX Group Securities is prohibited.

clearance.approver: Direct manager or senior leadership team member, whichever is most senior; alternate the Group Executive, failing which an alternate determined by Enterprise Risk and Compliance
clearance.evidence: ASX pre-clearance is obtained by using the specified online form available on ASX's intranet. ... You must deal within five business days once ASX pre-clearance approval has been granted.

clearance.tier: ASX Limited and CS facility licensee Non-Executive Directors
clearance.approver: Chair, ASX Limited (alternate: Group General Counsel or Chief Risk Officer); for the Chair of ASX Limited, the Chair of the Board Risk Committee (alternate: Chair, People and Culture Committee)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: All NED dealings in ASX Group Securities, where permitted, irrespective of whether there has or has not been a change of the underlying beneficial holding, must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days.

clearance.approver: Chair, ASX Limited (alternate: Group General Counsel or Chief Risk Officer)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (any derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities; may be publicly disclosed)
clearance.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.

clearance.approver: Direct manager or senior leadership team member, whichever is most senior; the CEO is cleared by the Chair of ASX Limited having consulted the Group General Counsel or Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (any derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities; may be publicly disclosed)
clearance.evidence: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities.

clearance.tier: Chief Compliance Officer and people in Listings Compliance, the Market Announcements Office and Surveillance
clearance.approver: For the Chief Compliance Officer, the CEO or Group General Counsel (alternate: Chair or Deputy Chair, Board Risk Committee); otherwise the direct manager or senior leadership team member
clearance.evidence: The Chief Compliance Officer and people in Listings Compliance, the Market Announcements Office and Surveillance and their Connected Persons, must not hold, deal in or have an interest in Covered Securities except when: ... dealing in ASX Group securities during designated ASX Trading Windows – provided ASX pre-clearance has been received.

clearance.approver: The same authorisation officer as for the related ASX person
clearance.evidence: ASX People must ensure their Connected Persons comply with this Policy.

short_term.basis: purchase then sale, or sale then purchase, of Covered Securities of the same entity
short_term.evidence: You must not purchase then sell (and inversely sell and then purchase) any Covered Securities of the same entity within a three-month period.

short_term.tier: ASX Limited and CS facility licensee Non-Executive Directors
short_term.basis: dealing in ASX Group Securities within a three-month period
short_term.evidence: Short-term dealing (that is, within a three-month period) in ASX Group Securities is prohibited.

exceptions.approver: General Manager, Enterprise Risk and Compliance (alternate: Chief Risk Officer or Group General Counsel); for NEDs, the Chair of ASX Limited (alternate: Chair of an ASX Board Committee)
exceptions.evidence: You may request a waiver from this Policy's dealing prohibitions in certain exceptional circumstances, including: severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: General Manager, Enterprise Risk and Compliance
exceptions.evidence: a transfer pursuant to the terms of a family law property settlement, and a testamentary disposition.
participation in ASX Group's Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP), noting you are only permitted to make an election change during an ASX Trading Window
acceptance of a takeover offer or participation in a scheme of arrangement
transfers where there is no underlying change to the beneficial owner of the Covered Securities.

You do not require clearance for grants, allocations or vesting of shares, rights or awards you receive under an ASX Employee Share Plan (ASX ESP). However, you must obtain pre-clearance to dispose of any such ASX Group Securities.
entering a margin loan or other financing arrangement over non-ASX Group Securities
participation in, or changes to an election in relation to, a corporate action in connection with non-ASX Group Securities.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price triggers are specified. Instead the holder must take all reasonable steps to ensure the terms of any margin loan or financing arrangement neither require nor allow ASX Group Securities to be disposed of at a time that would breach the Policy, such as outside a designated ASX Trading Window.

exemption_authority: Waivers from the Policy's dealing prohibitions may be granted in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, a transfer under a family law property settlement, a testamentary disposition) where the proposed dealing is the only reasonable course of action available and the applicant holds no Inside Information; waivers may be conditional. Granted by the General Manager, Enterprise Risk and Compliance (alternate Chief Risk Officer or Group General Counsel) for ASX people and Connected Persons; by the CEO or Group General Counsel for the Chief Compliance Officer; by the Chair of ASX Limited (having consulted the Group General Counsel or Company Secretary) for the CEO; and by the Chair of ASX Limited for ASX Limited and subsidiary NEDs. Requests go to enterprise.compliance@asx.com.au.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement. You must ensure any portfolio of Covered Securities provided as collateral does not comprise ASX Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar outright, including the technique of pledging a diversified portfolio that happens to contain ASX shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: financing terms must not allow out-of-window sales
bespoke_clauses.clause: You must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the terms of your margin loan or financing arrangement does not require, nor allow for, ASX Group Securities to be disposed of at such time that would breach this Policy, such as outside of a designated ASX Trading Window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a lawful financing arrangement must be documented so that the lender has no right to sell ASX shares outside a Trading Window, which rules out ordinary bank enforcement and margin-call mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging vested shares is permitted but disclosable
bespoke_clauses.clause: ASX Group Executives and ASX Group Directors must notify the Company Secretary if they enter a derivative or hedging position over vested ASX Group Securities. This may be publicly disclosed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The unfunded collar over vested, unlocked shares is permitted, but the executive must accept notification and possible public disclosure of the position.

bespoke_clauses.topic: holding lock extends the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from entering a transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested ASX Group Securities or vested ASX Group Securities that are subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting alone is not enough; any holding lock on the shares must have lifted before they can be included in the collared parcel.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC instruments fall outside Covered Securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities: Any financial product quoted on a financial market. Covered Securities: Financial products quoted on an Australian financial market, including shares, options, derivatives, warrants, futures debentures, hybrids and single-entity ETPs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An over-the-counter put or call is not a Covered Security, so the pre-clearance and Trading Window machinery does not by its terms apply to the derivative legs, only the express hedging rule and the notification obligation do, but the 'letter and spirit' clause makes it prudent to pre-clear anyway.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You may request a waiver from this Policy's dealing prohibitions in certain exceptional circumstances, including: severe financial hardship ... The proposed dealing is to be the only reasonable course of action available to you and any granted waiver may be subject to conditions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only conceivable route to a secured facility, but it is limited to exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course available, so it cannot support an ordinary liquidity or diversification collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The ASX Board may decline to open a Trading Window during the periods listed above. The ASX Board may also elect to shorten, change or close a ASX Trading Window at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no guaranteed window, so any collar entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement can be blocked at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Pre-clearance to deal may be denied for any reason, including, but not limited, to: ... matters known to ASX, but not to you, and your ASX authorisation officer determines pre-clearance should not be granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on the executive being able to trade at any particular time, and no reason for a refusal need be given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy contains a set of principles. You must comply with both the letter and spirit of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A structure engineered around the definition of Covered Securities to escape pre-clearance is exposed to challenge on spirit grounds even if the literal wording permits it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: CS licensee directors cannot hold at all
bespoke_clauses.clause: For NEDs appointed to the Boards of the ASX Clearing & Settlement facility licensees, the holding of ASX Group securities is prohibited.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For that group there is no underlying shareholding at all, so no collar, funded or otherwise, is possible.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Connected Persons are ASX peoples' spouse, de facto partner, children residing with the ASX person, and companies, trusts, Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs) or other entities controlled by an ASX person and/or their Connected Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares in a family trust, company or SMSF does not avoid the collateral ban or the pre-clearance and window regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must deal within five business days once ASX pre-clearance approval has been granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared leg must be executed within five business days, which is workable for a negotiated OTC trade but leaves no room for extended documentation.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for an ASX Limited director or executive, although the derivative legs alone are. Section 2.5 expressly permits transactions limiting economic risk over vested ASX Group Securities that are not subject to a holding lock, banning them only over unvested or holding-locked securities, and the only formality for ASX Group Executives and Directors is notification to the Company Secretary, with possible public disclosure; the OTC legs are not themselves Covered Securities, though the Policy's 'letter and spirit' clause makes pre-clearance prudent and any exchange-traded leg would require it, be executable only within five business days and confined to a Trading Window opened at the ASX Board's discretion after half-year results, full-year results and the AGM. The loan leg fails outright: ASX people are prohibited from using ASX Group Securities as collateral when entering a new margin loan or other financing arrangement, and must ensure that any collateral portfolio contains no ASX Group Securities. The Policy goes further and requires that the terms of any financing arrangement neither require nor allow ASX Group Securities to be disposed of outside a Trading Window, which would rule out conventional lender enforcement and margin-call rights even if collateral were permitted. The only conceivable route is a section 2.8 waiver from Enterprise Risk and Compliance or the Chair for severe financial hardship where the dealing is the only reasonable course available, which will not support an ordinary liquidity or diversification collar, and Non-Executive Directors of the Clearing & Settlement facility licensees may not hold ASX Group securities at all.
